Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Free radical chlorination of toluene at $383\text{ K}$ gives benzal chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHCl}_2$). Hydrolysis of gem-dichlorides produces an unstable gem-diol that dehydrates to benzaldehyde (commercial preparation of benzaldehyde). Because benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogens, heating it with concentrated ($50\%$) $\text{NaOH}$ causes it to undergo the Cannizzaro disproportionation reaction, quantitatively yielding an equimolar mixture of benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Aldol condensation fundamentally requires an $\alpha$-hydrogen atom on a $sp^3$-carbon adjacent to the carbonyl. Benzaldehyde has no $\alpha$-hydrogens. The formyl hydrogen attached directly to the carbonyl carbon is not acidic and cannot be abstracted by $\text{OH}^-$ to form an enolate. Thus, benzaldehyde undergoes Cannizzaro reaction, not aldol condensation. Therefore, Reason (R) is completely false.
Step 3: Conclude that Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match the reaction sequences in List I with their corresponding major organic products specified in List II:
List I:
(P) $\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH} \xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+} / \text{dil. }\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4, 333\text{ K}}$
(Q) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{(i) DIBAL-H, } -78^\circ\text{C}, \text{(ii) }\text{H}_2\text{O}}$
(R) $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \xrightarrow{\text{(i) }\text{Br}_2 / \text{red P}, \text{(ii) }\text{H}_2\text{O}}$
(S) $2\text{CH}_3\text{COOK (aq)} \xrightarrow{\text{Kolbe electrolysis (anode)}}$
List II:
(1) 2-Bromopropanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH(Br)-COOH}$)
(2) Ethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CH}_3$)
(3) Propan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3$)
(4) Propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{-CHO}$)
Choose the correct matching from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Match (P): Hydration of propyne with $\text{HgSO}_4 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ follows Markovnikov addition of water to give an unstable enol, prop-1-en-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)=CH}_2$), which tautomerises exclusively to propan-2-one (acetone) $\rightarrow$ matches (3).
Step 2: Match (Q): Selective reduction of methyl propanoate with DIBAL-H at $-78^\circ\text{C}$ followed by hydrolysis yields propanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$) $\rightarrow$ matches (4).
Step 3: Match (R): Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) bromination of propanoic acid using $\text{Br}_2 / \text{red P}$ replaces the $\alpha$-hydrogen with bromine, furnishing 2-bromopropanoic acid $\rightarrow$ matches (1).
Step 4: Match (S): Kolbe's electrolytic decarboxylation of aqueous potassium ethanoate yields acetate radicals at the anode, which lose $\text{CO}_2$ to generate methyl radicals; dimerization of methyl radicals produces ethane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_3$) $\rightarrow$ matches (2).
Step 5: Combining these matches gives P-3, Q-4, R-1, S-2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements regarding the hydration equilibria of carbonyl compounds and the structural stability of chloral hydrate:
Statement I: While most aldehydes and ketones form gem-diols that are thermodynamically unstable and spontaneously dehydrate back to carbonyls in solution, the equilibrium position for formaldehyde ($\text{HCHO}$) in water lies predominantly ($>99\%$) towards the gem-diol (methanediol).
Statement II: Chloral hydrate ($\text{CCl}_3\text{-CH(OH)}_2$) can be isolated as a stable, crystalline solid because intramolecular hydrogen bonding between the hydroxyl hydrogens and the chlorine atoms forms stable five-membered rings that counteract the steric crowding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
B) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Statement I. The position of hydration equilibrium ($\text{>C=O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{>C(OH)}_2$) depends on steric relief and relief of electronic strain. In formaldehyde, the carbonyl carbon has no electron-donating alkyl groups and small hydrogen substituents; hydration relieves angle strain from $120^\circ$ to $109.5^\circ$. Consequently, $K_{\text{eq}} \approx 2000$, and formal aqueous formalin exists over $99.9\%$ as methanediol. Thus, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Analyze Statement II. Chloral (trichloroethanal, $\text{CCl}_3\text{CHO}$) has three powerfully electron-withdrawing chlorine atoms ($-I$) that make the carbonyl carbon exceptionally electrophilic. Upon addition of water, chloral forms chloral hydrate, $\text{CCl}_3\text{-CH(OH)}_2$. This gem-diol is uniquely stable and can be isolated as a crystalline solid due to two factors: (i) strong $-I$ dispersion of charge, and (ii) intramolecular hydrogen bonds ($\text{O-H}\cdots\text{Cl}$) forming five-membered chelate rings that stabilize the hydroxyl groups against spontaneous elimination of water. Thus, Statement II is correct.
Step 3: Conclude that both statements are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Carboxylic acids do not give characteristic nucleophilic addition reactions of carbonyl compounds, failing to form oximes with hydroxylamine or bisulphite adducts with sodium hydrogen sulphite.
Reason (R): The unshared lone pair of electrons on the hydroxyl oxygen atom is delocalised into the carbonyl group via resonance, significantly diminishing the electrophilic character of the carbonyl carbon.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Despite containing a formal carbon-oxygen double bond ($\text{>C=O}$), carboxylic acids do not undergo typical nucleophilic addition reactions characteristic of aldehydes and ketones. They fail to react with hydroxylamine (to form oximes), semicarbazide, 2,4-DNP, or sodium hydrogen sulphite. Thus, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). In a carboxylic acid, the lone pair on the hydroxyl oxygen participates in resonance with the adjacent carbonyl $\pi$-system: $$\text{R-C(=O)-OH} \longleftrightarrow \text{R-C(O}^-\text{)=O}^+\text{H}$$
This resonance electron donation from the hydroxyl oxygen directly satisfies the electron deficiency of the carbonyl carbon, drastically reducing its partial positive charge ($\delta^+$). Because the carbonyl carbon is far less electrophilic than that in aldehydes and ketones, weak nucleophiles cannot attack it. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Benzoic acid and benzaldehyde readily undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride to give high yields of substituted products.
Reason (R): The catalyst anhydrous aluminium chloride ($\text{AlCl}_3$) is a Lewis acid that coordinates strongly to the lone pairs of the carbonyl oxygen, and the strongly electron-withdrawing carbonyl group severely deactivates the aromatic ring toward electrophilic attack.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Aromatic aldehydes, ketones, and carboxylic acids (such as benzaldehyde and benzoic acid) do NOT undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation reactions. Any attempt to carry out Friedel-Crafts reactions on them results in no reaction. Thus, Assertion (A) is completely false.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). There are two reasons for this failure: (i) The carbonyl/carboxyl group ($\text{-CHO}$, $\text{-COOH}$) is strongly deactivating toward electrophilic aromatic substitution due to its strong $-I$ and $-R$ electron-withdrawing effects. (ii) The Lewis acid catalyst (anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$) coordinates tightly to the basic oxygen atom of the carbonyl group rather than generating the electrophile, which places a full positive charge adjacent to the benzene ring and further deactivates it completely. Thus, Reason (R) is true.
Step 3: Conclude that Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
